claims: President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026.
Pam Bondi had a 14-month tenure as Attorney General.
President Trump described the firing of Pam Bondi as a transition.
Pam Bondi faced intense criticism for her management of the release of Jeffrey Epstein files.
The released Jeffrey Epstein files were heavily redacted.
The release of Jeffrey Epstein files did not lead to major prosecutions.
Pam Bondi appeared to contradict other administration officials.
President Trump felt that Pam Bondi failed to sufficiently investigate and prosecute his political enemies.
There were efforts to align the Department of Justice with President Trump's personal agenda.
A heated confrontation occurred at the White House last week.
Pam Bondi was facing a scheduled deposition by the House Oversight Committee regarding the Epstein investigation.
Pam Bondi was replaced by her deputy Todd Blanche on an interim basis
